tomato.affected_plant_part: Leaves, flower buds, green and ripe fruits
tomato.damage_symptoms: Larvae bore round circular holes into tomato fruits and feed while keeping anterior body inside and posterior outside; fruits rot and drop prematurely.
tomato.favourable_conditions: Warm days (26-32°C), moderate relative humidity, presence of alternate hosts (pigeonpea, cotton, chickpea).
tomato.affected_diseases: None directly transmitted (bore holes predispose fruits to secondary fungal/bacterial soft rot)
tomato.management: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 50,000/ha; spray HaNPV (Helicoverpa nuclear polyhedrosis virus) @ 250 LE/ha with 1% jaggery; application of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3ml/L (PHI: 3 days) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L.
tomato.prevention: Intercrop with African Marigold (1 row marigold for every 16 rows tomato) as trap crop; install pheromone traps (Helilure @ 5/acre).

tomato.affected_plant_part: Underside of tender leaves, growing shoots
tomato.damage_symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck cell sap from leaf undersides causing chlorotic stippling and downward leaf curling; heavy honeydew excretion leads to black sooty mold.
tomato.favourable_conditions: Warm dry conditions (28-35°C), low relative humidity (<60%), dry spells during post-monsoon.
tomato.cause_relationship: Pest vectors and transmits plant pathogenic virus
tomato.management: Spray neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2ml/L; release predatory lacewings Chrysoperla zastrowi @ 10,000/ha; spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.25g/L or Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2g/L.
tomato.prevention: Install yellow sticky traps (15-20/acre) at canopy level; grow border crop of 2 rows of maize or pearl millet as live barrier; use 40-mesh insect-proof netting in nurseries.

tomato.affected_plant_part: Undersurface of older and middle leaves
tomato.damage_symptoms: Mites puncture plant cells on leaf undersurface causing fine white or yellow speckles (stippling); leaves turn bronzed and dry; fine silky webbing covers terminals.
tomato.favourable_conditions: Hot and dry climate (30-38°C), dusty field borders, prolonged drought stress.
tomato.management: Foliar wash with water jets to knock down mites; spray wettable sulphur 80% WP @ 3g/L or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1ml/L or Abamectin 1.9% EC @ 0.75ml/L.
tomato.prevention: Avoid water stress in crops; maintain good weed sanitation; avoid broad-spectrum pyrethroid insecticides which eliminate predatory phytoseiid mites.

paddy.affected_plant_part: Base of tillers, leaf sheath above water line
paddy.damage_symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck sap from tiller bases causing circular patches of dry, burnt crops called 'hopper burn'.
paddy.favourable_conditions: High nitrogen application, dense planting, prolonged high humidity (>85%), stagnant standing water.
paddy.cause_relationship: Pest vectors and transmits plant pathogenic virus
paddy.affected_diseases: Rice Grassy Stunt Virus & Rice Ragged Stunt Virus
paddy.management: Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) irrigation; drain water for 3-4 days; conserve mirid bug Cyrtorhinus lividipennis; spray Triflumezopyrim 10% SC @ 0.48ml/L or Pymetrozine 50% WDG @ 0.6g/L directed strictly at the base.
paddy.prevention: Adopt wider spacing (20x15 cm) with alleyways (2m paths); avoid synthetic pyrethroid sprays which kill predatory spiders.

paddy.damage_symptoms: Larvae bore into stem and feed on inner tissue; causes 'dead hearts' (drying of central tiller) in vegetative stage and 'white ears' (chaffy erect white panicles) in reproductive stage.
paddy.favourable_conditions: Stagnant deep water, night temperatures 20-26°C, continuous staggered planting.
paddy.management: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma japonicum @ 1,00,000/ha at weekly intervals; apply Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR @ 10kg/ha in standing water or Cartap Hydrochloride 50% SP @ 2g/L.
paddy.prevention: Clip tip of rice seedlings before transplanting to eliminate egg masses; install sex pheromone traps @ 5/acre.

chilli.affected_plant_part: Under-surface of leaves, growing tips, flowers
chilli.damage_symptoms: Lacerate tender leaf tissues and suck oozing sap; leaves curl upwards into boat-shapes with roughened brown necrotic streaks on leaf undersides; causes 'murda' condition.
chilli.favourable_conditions: Hot and dry weather, absence of rain showers, temperatures 30-37°C.
chilli.cause_relationship: Pest vectors and transmits plant pathogenic virus
chilli.affected_diseases: Peanut Yellow Spot Virus / Chilli Tospo virus
chilli.management: Spray Lecanicillium lecanii @ 5g/L; apply Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.3ml/L or Fipronil 5% SC @ 2ml/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.25g/L (PHI: 7 days).
chilli.prevention: Intercrop with sorghum or maize as barrier crop; install blue sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre); spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%).
chilli.source: ANGRAU Regional Agricultural Research Station (Lam, Guntur) & TNAU

cotton.affected_plant_part: Squares, flower buds, green bolls, lint and seeds
cotton.damage_symptoms: Rosetted flowers that fail to open; entry holes in bolls heal over leaving no external sign, but larvae feed inside seeds, staining and destroying lint fiber; premature boll opening.
cotton.favourable_conditions: Late planted cotton, extended crop duration beyond 160 days, warm and humid post-monsoon weather.
cotton.management: Trichogrammatoidea bactrae release @ 1,50,000/ha; spray Beauveria bassiana @ 5g/L; apply Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3ml/L upon crossing ETL (8 moths/trap/day for 3 days).
cotton.prevention: Strictly terminate crop within 150-160 days to break pest lifecycle; install pink bollworm pheromone traps (Gossyplure @ 5/acre); avoid storing cotton stalks in fields.

cotton.damage_symptoms: Sucking sap leads to leaf chlorosis and premature leaf drop; dense honeydew promotes sooty mold on lint.
cotton.favourable_conditions: Warm and dry conditions (30-36°C) with low rainfall, high nitrogen fertilization.
cotton.cause_relationship: Pest vectors and transmits plant pathogenic virus
cotton.management: Spray neem oil 1500 ppm @ 3ml/L; spray Pyriproxyfen 10% EC @ 1ml/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.25g/L or Afidopyropen 50 g/L @ 2ml/L.
cotton.prevention: Install yellow sticky traps (10/acre); avoid excessive urea applications; grow resistant/tolerant hybrids.

sugarcane.affected_plant_part: Shoots of young cane (1 to 3 months old)
sugarcane.damage_symptoms: Larva bores into base of young shoot just below soil level and feeds inside; central growing shoot dries up into an easily-pulled 'dead heart' emitting an offensive decaying smell.
sugarcane.favourable_conditions: High temperatures (35-40°C), low relative humidity, light sandy soils, drought stress during early vegetative phase.
sugarcane.management: Release Trichogramma chilonis @ 50,000/ha from 4th week of planting at 10-day intervals; spray Granulosis virus (ESB-GV) @ 1.5x10^8 IBS/ml; apply Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR @ 18.75kg/ha at planting or spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3ml/L at 30 days.
sugarcane.prevention: Plant setts in deep furrows; trash mulching @ 5 tonnes/ha on ridges within 3 days of planting; earthing up at 45 days.

maize.affected_plant_part: Leaf whorl, tassel, ear silks, developing kernels
maize.damage_symptoms: Young larvae scrape epidermal layer creating papery pinholes; older larvae feed inside leaf whorl causing heavy ragged windowing and leaving prominent piles of wet sawdust-like fecal frass; inverted Y mark on head.
maize.favourable_conditions: Warm and semi-arid conditions (26-34°C), prolonged dry spells followed by rain.
maize.management: Release egg parasitoid Telenomus remus @ 1,25,000/ha; spray Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki @ 2g/L or Metarhizium rileyi @ 3g/L; apply Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4ml/L or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L directed into the central whorl.
maize.prevention: Synchronous planting in village clusters; erect bird perches (10/acre); apply sand and wood ash (9:1) directly into whorls; install FAW pheromone traps @ 5/acre.

coconut.affected_plant_part: Crown heart, unopened fronds and spathes
coconut.damage_symptoms: Adult beetle bores into crown heart and chews unopened fronds; when damaged fronds unfold, leaflets display distinctive V-shaped geometric notches or clipped shears appearance.
coconut.favourable_conditions: Nearby rotting organic manure pits, decaying coconut stumps and coir dust mounds acting as breeding sites.
coconut.cause_relationship: Pest infestation/damage (feeding wounds facilitate entry of secondary fungal pathogens)
coconut.affected_diseases: Thielaviopsis paradoxa (Stem Bleeding / Bud Rot predisposition)
coconut.management: Maintain orchard sanitation; treat manure pits with Metarhizium anisopliae green muscardine fungus @ 5x10^11 spores/m3; hook out beetles using an iron rod with curved needle; crown placement of naphthalene balls (approx 10g) mixed with fine sand in uppermost 3 leaf axils.
coconut.prevention: Regular field inspection; destroy dead palm trunks; incorporate Metarhizium into FYM compost heaps.

coffee.affected_plant_part: Main stem, thick primary branches of Arabica coffee
coffee.damage_symptoms: Grub tunnels inside hardwood causing characteristic external ridges/rings on trunk bark; leaves yellow, wilt and dry out; bearing branches snap easily; killed bushes.
coffee.favourable_conditions: Open unshaded coffee patches, bright sunlight directly hitting main stems, post-monsoon warm dry periods.
coffee.management: Bark scraping of loose scaly bark on main stems before flight season to dislodge eggs; install cross-vane pheromone traps; stem swabbing/spraying with registered adhesive formulation up to 1.5m prior to beetle flight; trace, uproot and burn infested bushes.
coffee.prevention: Maintain optimal two-tier shade (40-50% canopy shade); wrap/band main stem with plastic sheets during flight periods.
